questions.q: In Purview's permission model, what do you typically assign a user or security group to?
options: An individual role, directly, almost always
A role group, which bundles roles matching a real job function
Nothing — Purview has no concept of roles
A single Azure subscription
questions.explain: You almost never assign a lone role to a lone user. Members get added to a role group — a bundle of roles matching a real job function — and inherit every role inside it.

questions.q: Where do you manage role groups, roles, and members in the Microsoft Purview portal?
options: Settings → Roles and scopes
The Exchange admin center only
A separate, unrelated Azure resource
You cannot manage this from inside the Purview portal at all
questions.explain: Settings → Roles and scopes is where you manage Role groups, Roles, Members, and check your own access under My permissions.

questions.q: Who can view and edit role groups in the Microsoft Purview portal?
options: Any user with a Purview license
A Global Administrator, or a user assigned the Role Management role (via the Organization Management role group)
Only Microsoft support engineers
Anyone who created the Purview account, forever, regardless of later role changes
questions.explain: Viewing Role groups requires being a Global Administrator or holding the Role Management role, which is assigned only through the Organization Management role group — a deliberately narrow gate.

questions.q: What does the 'Assign admin units' option do when editing a role group's members?
options: It deletes the role group entirely
It restricts that member's role group assignment to one or more Microsoft Entra administrative units instead of the whole tenant
It grants the member Global Administrator access
It has no effect on scope, only on billing
questions.explain: Assign admin units scopes a role group assignment to specific administrative units (like a region or department), making that administrator a 'restricted administrator' who can only see and manage data for their assigned unit(s).

questions.q: If a user holds both a scoped Purview role group assignment (restricted to one administrative unit) and the same role as a tenant-wide Microsoft Entra role, what is their effective access?
options: Restricted to the administrative unit only, since the scoped assignment always wins
No access at all, since the two conflict
Unscoped — the Microsoft Entra role takes precedence, and the administrative-unit restriction is effectively ignored for anything the two roles overlap on
They must choose one role to keep and must have the other manually removed
questions.explain: Per this lesson, Entra roles take precedence at runtime. If a user has both a scoped Purview assignment and the same role unscoped in Entra, their effective access becomes unscoped wherever the two overlap.
